name: Isolated Humeral Agenesis/Hypoplasia

criteria.description: Radiological absence of the humerus bone in one or both upper limbs
Presence of normal or near-normal forearm and hand bones without other limb malformations
No associated systemic or syndromic abnormalities on clinical and genetic evaluation
Clinical assessment showing functional impairment localized to the humeral segment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiological humeral agenesis or severe hypoplasia with normal distal limb structures and absence of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological and clinical; genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic causes.

searchTerms: absence of upper arm bone at birth
one arm longer than the other

common.symptomName: Compensatory forearm and hand function adaptation
searchTerms: using forearm and hand differently to compensate
adjusted arm movements to overcome weakness

common.symptomName: Mild muscle hypoplasia around the shoulder girdle
searchTerms: reduced muscle bulk near shoulder girdle

occasional.symptomName: Mild scoliosis due to limb length discrepancy
searchTerms: mild spine curvature from uneven limb length
slight scoliosis due to arm length difference
spinal tilt caused by limb length mismatch

occasional.symptomName: Mild functional impairment of fine motor skills
searchTerms: slight difficulty with fine hand movements
mild problems with precise finger use

occasional.symptomName: Localized soft tissue contractures around the shoulder
searchTerms: localized muscle or tendon tightening near shoulder
restricted shoulder movement from tissue contracture

rare.symptomName: Mild limb length discrepancy in contralateral arm
searchTerms: slight length difference in opposite arm
mild arm length mismatch on other side

rare.symptomName: Transient nerve compression symptoms due to altered anatomy
searchTerms: brief numbness or tingling from anatomy changes
transient nerve irritation due to bone structure

imaging: X-ray showing absent or hypoplastic humerus
MRI to assess soft tissue and muscle involvement
Ultrasound to exclude vascular or nerve anomalies
genetic: No consistent pathogenic variants identified; genetic testing used to exclude syndromic causes
other: Clinical functional assessment of upper limb mobility and strength

distinguishingFeatures: Severe shortening or absence of proximal and distal limb segments
Often associated with syndromic features or teratogenic exposure
Complete absence of one or more limbs rather than isolated humeral involvement
Frequently associated with other congenital anomalies
Involvement of radius and thumb abnormalities
Often syndromic with hematological or cardiac anomalies

redFlags: Presence of systemic or syndromic features suggesting broader congenital syndrome
Progressive neurological deficits in affected limb
Severe functional impairment requiring urgent intervention
references: Rosenberg HK, et al. Congenital absence of the humerus: clinical and radiological features. J Pediatr Orthop. 2018.
